newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal cement privatisation set for mid-October.
newsitem.headline: Portugal cement privatisation set for mid-October.

text.p: State-controlled cement company Cimpor said on Monday that the next phase of its privatisation, one of the biggest planned by the Portuguese government this year, had been set for next month.
"It will be October 15," a company spokeswoman said.
The government has yet to give a full timetable for the sale of up to 45 percent of Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal SA, which could be worth more than 120 billion escudos ($775 million).
It has said there will be a pre-registration period for investors to declare an interest in buying the stock ahead of the formal subscription period.

Shares in Cimpor, 20 percent of which is already listed, lost two percent of their value to 3,312 escudos on Monday after company chairman Antonio Sousa Gomes described the current price as expensive.

The Portuguese government is well on the way to raising the $2.5 billion it wants to earn from privatisations in 1996 after selling a further chunk of Portugal Telecom and its holding in Banco de Fomento & Exterior. ($1=154.71 escudos)
